# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
# check=skip=InvalidDefaultArgInFrom
#
# cogmo-devbase — base task-container image for coding-delegation.
#
# Built and published as the `devbase` target of `/docker-bake.hcl` by
# .github/workflows/publish.yml at every cogmo release. Tag tracks the
# cogmo app version, so `cogmo:1.46.0` always pairs with
# `cogmo-devbase:1.46.0`. See design/coding-delegation.md → "Base Image"
# for the full contract.
#
# Today's image ships what plan-only Claude Code flows need plus the uv
# toolchain skill-authoring tasks rely on (`uv pip compile` to produce a
# `requirements.lock` byte-identical to what `cogmo-skills` resolves at
# register time):
#   - Node 26 + pnpm + git + gh + ripgrep + fd + jq + curl
#   - @anthropic-ai/claude-code (pinned)
#   - Python 3 (from devcontainers/base) + uv (pinned to match cogmo-skills)
#   - Non-root user `vscode` (UID 1000) inherited from the devcontainers base.
#
# Codex CLI and Go/Rust toolchains are deferred to whenever real verify
# commands need them.

# Toolchain versions come from docker-bake.hcl alone. No ARG carries a
# default, so a build outside bake fails at the uv FROM below, and each
# install expands its version with `:?` because npm reads an empty one as
# `latest`.
#
# uv and pnpm come in as stages copied from their official images. ARGs in a
# FROM need global scope, so they precede the first one. uv is shared with
# cogmo-skills.
ARG UV_VERSION=0.13.7
ARG UV_DIGEST=sha256:96f40d3904aad8d0bd010539001d36c8e2188b981e1334471a90c4a1d93bb490
ARG PNPM_VERSION=12.17.0
ARG PNPM_DIGEST=sha256:172468925f0ca368313c09867081a43e298eaeb13dee8f7e4356bfad45dd8b15
FROM ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:${UV_VERSION}@${UV_DIGEST} AS uv
FROM ghcr.io/pnpm/pnpm:${PNPM_VERSION}@${PNPM_DIGEST} AS pnpm

FROM mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/base:ubuntu-24.04@sha256:d94c97dd9cacf183d0a6fd12a8e87b526e9e928307674ae9c94139139c0c6eae

# Make `RUN ... | ...` fail when any element of the pipe fails. The
# nodesource install (`curl ... | bash -`) below silently succeeds on a
# truncated curl without this.
SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-o", "pipefail", "-c"]

ARG NPM_VERSION=12.2.2
ARG PNPM_VERSION=12.17.0
ARG CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=2.1.311

# devcontainers/base already ships git, gh, curl, jq, ripgrep — but `fd-find`
# is missing on Ubuntu and the binary is named `fdfind` rather than `fd`.
#
# `apt-get upgrade` applies Ubuntu security updates that landed after the
# upstream rebuild — the devcontainers base image trails published USN
# advisories by days to weeks and accumulates a large CVE surface on the
# `ubuntu-24.04` tag. Hadolint's DL3005 disagrees with this on the premise
# that maintainers keep base images patched; in practice they don't, and
# this image runs inside sysbox sandboxes where every patch we can apply
# at build time tightens the userland surface.
# hadolint ignore=DL3005
RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get upgrade -y \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends fd-find \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
 && ln -s /usr/bin/fdfind /usr/local/bin/fd

# Node 26 LTS via NodeSource. Upgrade npm past the bundled version — its
# bundled deps (picomatch / ip-address / brace-expansion) lag upstream and
# show up as image CVEs.
RUN curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_26.x | bash - \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends nodejs \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
 && npm install -g "npm@${NPM_VERSION:?}" \
 && npm cache clean --force

# pnpm is a native executable, plus the `dist/` it reads beside the resolved
# executable (its bundled node-gyp). `pnpx` and `pnx` are `pnpm dlx`. A symlink
# to the binary runs plain `pnpm`, so each is a script. A tag beside a digest
# is ignored, so the version check catches a PNPM_VERSION bumped without
# PNPM_DIGEST.
COPY --from=pnpm --chown=root:root /opt/pnpm /opt/pnpm
RUN ln -s /opt/pnpm/pnpm /usr/local/bin/pnpm \
 && ln -s /opt/pnpm/pnpm /usr/local/bin/pn \
 && for alias in pnpx pnx; do \
      printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec /opt/pnpm/pnpm dlx "$@"\n' > "/usr/local/bin/$alias" \
      && chmod 755 "/usr/local/bin/$alias"; \
    done \
 && test "$(pnpm --version)" = "${PNPM_VERSION:?}"

# Claude Code CLI. npm blocks install scripts unless the package is named in
# `--allow-scripts`, independently of `ignore-scripts`. Claude Code ships a
# thin JS wrapper plus a per-platform native binary as an optional dependency,
# and its postinstall is what puts that binary in place — without the
# allowlist the install "succeeds" and `claude` then fails at runtime with
# "native binary not installed". Naming the one package we intend to trust
# keeps the default deny for everything else in the tree.
RUN npm install -g --allow-scripts=@anthropic-ai/claude-code "@anthropic-ai/claude-code@${CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION:?}" \
 && claude --version \
 && npm cache clean --force

# uv — shared pin with cogmo-skills so author-side `uv pip compile` produces
# lockfiles byte-identical to what cogmo-skills re-resolves at register time.
COPY --from=uv /uv /uvx /usr/local/bin/

# Drop privileges. Cogmo's supervisor mounts the worktree at /workspace and
# always overrides Entrypoint/Cmd at create-container time, so we leave the
# image's default entrypoint alone (devcontainers/base provides one suitable
# for `docker run` smoke tests).
USER vscode
WORKDIR /workspace

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"# Task
Create a new skill named "btc-spot" in the skills repo.

Create a folder for the skill containing:
1. SKILL.md — manifest with: name "btc-spot", a short description ("Fetches the current Bitcoin spot price in USD from CoinGecko"), tier "notify" (read-only network effect, no secrets, no acting effect), network.allow listing "api.coingecko.com", and inputs: none (skill takes no input). Do NOT list any dependencies in SKILL.md.
2. skill.py — a single module-level async function `async def run(inputs, ctx)` (or with no Input model if none needed, following the pattern: if no Input class, define run to take exactly two parameters). It should:
   - Call `result = await ctx.http.get("https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/simple/price?ids=bitcoin&vs_currencies=usd")`
   - Parse `result['body']` with `json.loads` (import json standard library only)
   - Extract the bitcoin USD price from the parsed JSON (structure: {"bitcoin": {"usd": <number>}})
   - Return `{"price": <number>}` (a dict, or an Output pydantic model with a single `price: float` field — whichever matches the simplest valid entrypoint pattern for this framework)
   - Do NOT use urllib, requests, httpx, or any third-party HTTP library — only `ctx.http.get`.
   - Do NOT create a requirements.lock file or declare any dependencies anywhere.

Keep it minimal and correct. Open a PR when done.

# Environment
- Repo root is /workspace. Stay inside it.
- Current branch: cogmo/01a1cb5822c2. Already created and checked out.
- Git credentials are NOT available in plan mode — you cannot push or pull.
- Do NOT make any edits. Plan only.

# Skills repo convention
- This is the skills library. One feature branch = exactly one skill.
- Each skill lives in `skills/<name>/`, `<name>` being its manifest's name: SKILL.md
  (the manifest), skill.py (the implementation), and (if the skill imports any
  third-party package) requirements.lock. Change only those files of the one skill:
  registration refuses skill files at the repo root, any other path, and a branch
  that changes more than one skill.
- skill.py's entrypoint, which register checks: `run` bound once, as one undecorated `async def run` directly at module level, taking exactly two parameters, none `*args`, `**kwargs` or keyword-only. With an `Input` or `Output` class, annotate `inputs: Input` and `-> Output` by their bare names.
  With pydantic models: `async def run(inputs: Input, ctx: Ctx) -> Output`, `Ctx` imported from `cogmo_ctx`.

SKILL.md frontmatter contract — these are validated structurally, not free-form:
  - The frontmatter is YAML. Any value containing `{`, `}`, `:`, `#`, `[`, or `]`
    MUST be wrapped in double quotes — otherwise YAML parses the special char as
    structure (e.g. unquoted `{ price: number }` becomes a nested flow mapping).
  - name: lowercase, starts with letter, [a-z0-9_-] only
  - description: 10-500 chars; quote it if it contains any YAML-special char above
  - tier: one of "wasm" | "container" (NOT "notify"/"approve" — those are risk tiers
    auto-derived from effects, not authored)
  - inputs: a JSON Schema object — must include `type: object` and (usually)
    `properties` + `required` arrays. Use `{type: object, properties: {}}` for
    no-arg skills. Never `inputs: none` or `inputs: <string>`. A skill whose
    skill.py defines a pydantic `Input` model omits `inputs`: register reads
    the model's schema and refuses both (likewise `outputs` beside an `Output`
    model). On a deployment that cannot import skills, register asks for
    `inputs` instead (`missing_inputs`); a skill.py that does not load is
    `schema_import_failed`, which `inputs` does not fix.
  - effects: an array of strings, picked from this closed set: reads_memory,
    writes_memory, reads_user_data, writes_user_data, sends_email, sends_message,
    posts_public, deletes_external, financial, reads_filesystem, writes_filesystem,
    spawns_subprocess. Use `[]` if none apply. Never a free-form string or a value
    outside this set. A read-only HTTP call to a public API needs no effects.
  - dependencies: an array of strict `name==version` strings. Required for any
    third-party import in skill.py. Use `[]` (or omit) when skill.py is stdlib-only.

Network access — the wasm tier (`tier: wasm`) has no sockets, so `urllib`, `http.client`,
`httpx` and `requests` cannot reach anything there and are rejected at register
time. Make requests through the host instead:
    `resp = await ctx.http.get(url)`  ->  {"status": int, "headers": dict, "body": str}
  `ctx.http.post(url, body, headers=...)` and `ctx.http.request(method, url, ...)`
  are also available. A 4xx/5xx comes back as a normal value carrying that
  status — check `resp["status"]` rather than catching. Parse with
  `json.loads(resp["body"])`. This needs no dependency and no lockfile.
  Reach for `tier: container` + `httpx` only when a vendor SDK is genuinely
  required; that tier has real sockets.
  Every host reached through `ctx.http` must be listed in the manifest, or
  the request is refused — with no `network:` block, `ctx.http` reaches
  nothing. (A `tier: container` skill calling httpx directly has real
  sockets and is not bound by this; prefer `ctx.http` there too.)
    network:
      allow:
        - api.example.com
        - '*.cdn.example.com'   # any depth under the zone; the apex needs its own entry
  List only the hosts actually contacted. A skill that declares both a secret
  and a network allowlist always needs human approval before it deploys, so
  keep the allowlist to what the skill uses.


Lockfile contract — if dependencies is non-empty:
- Generate requirements.lock in the skill's directory with `uv pip compile --no-header
  --generate-hashes -o skills/<name>/requirements.lock -` reading specs from stdin, e.g.:
    `printf 'httpx==0.27.2\n' | uv pip compile --no-header --generate-hashes
    -o skills/example-skill/requirements.lock -`
  uv is on PATH in the sandbox. The lockfile resolves transitive deps with
  hashes — register byte-compares against a fresh re-resolve, so `--no-header`
  is required (the header is non-deterministic).

Minimal valid skills/example-skill/SKILL.md (no deps):
```
---
name: example-skill
description: "One-line summary of what the skill does (at least 10 chars)."
tier: wasm
inputs:
  type: object
  properties: {}
effects: []
---
Free-form markdown body describing the skill in more detail.
```

Same shape with dependencies + a description that contains YAML-special chars:
```
---
name: example-skill
description: "Reads a row from the vendor API and returns { rows: number }."
tier: container
inputs:
  type: object
  properties: {}
effects: []
dependencies:
  - "httpx==0.27.2"
---
```

# Verify command (for context — runs after execution, not during plan)
uv run --locked --group dev .cogmo/verify

# Budget
Aim to keep the task within ~200000 tokens of execution. If the task is too large, narrow scope rather than promise the moon.

# When finished
Produce a "## Plan" section describing the steps you would take, the files you would touch, and how you would verify. Cogmo posts this plan to the human for approval before any execution. No edits, no commits, no pushes."}}

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
# check=skip=InvalidDefaultArgInFrom
#
# cogmo-skills — base task-container image for container-tier (sysbox) skills.
#
# Built and published as the `skills` target of `/docker-bake.hcl` by
# .github/workflows/publish.yml at every cogmo release. Tag tracks the
# cogmo app version. See `design/skills.md` → "Container tier — sysbox"
# for the contract.
#
# Built with uv: builder syncs the locked deps + builds the
# `cogmo_skills_runtime` package into a venv; runtime stage copies the
# venv AND the uv binary itself — register-time lockfile compile and
# first-invoke venv populate (see `design/skills.md` → Dependencies)
# both shell out to `uv` inside this image, so the runtime resolver
# matches the builder resolver byte-for-byte. The `tools` and `toolchain`
# stages build what register's CPython checks run: the skills repo
# toolchain's tools venv and its configuration.
#
# `cogmo_skills_runtime` itself has zero third-party python deps; only
# the per-skill venvs populated by `uv venv` + `uv pip sync` against a
# manifest's `requirements.lock` introduce wheels into the runtime.
#
# The `mutation` stage is a local test image for
# `pnpm test:mutation:skills`; the release build never reaches it.

# uv toolchain as a stage — version + digest from docker-bake.hcl, shared
# with cogmo-devbase. ARG-in-FROM needs global scope.
ARG UV_VERSION=0.13.7
ARG UV_DIGEST=sha256:96f40d3904aad8d0bd010539001d36c8e2188b981e1334471a90c4a1d93bb490
FROM ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:${UV_VERSION}@${UV_DIGEST} AS uv

FROM mirror.gcr.io/library/python:3.14.10-slim@sha256:af8a5aa14780025dbfbcfbc81bd8a91ebd87711dd5b0f48ed71090949dd7cb1d AS builder

COPY --from=uv /uv /uvx /bin/

ENV UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1
ENV UV_LINK_MODE=copy
ENV UV_NO_DEV=1
ENV UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=0
ENV UV_NO_EDITABLE=1

WORKDIR /app

# Lock-only sync first (without project source) — keeps the heavy deps
# layer cached when only src/ changes. README is required by hatchling
# for the package metadata even though we don't ship it. `.python-version`
# is the Python minor CI tests against; with downloads off, a FROM on any
# other minor fails this sync instead of shipping an untested runtime.
COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock README.md .python-version /app/
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
    uv sync --locked --no-install-project

# Now bring the package source and finalize the install.
COPY src /app/src/
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
    uv sync --locked --no-editable

# design/testing.md → Mutation Testing. The packages resolve to `/app/src`,
# which scripts/mutation.sh overlays with mutmut's mutated copy to re-run a
# mutant, so the `python -I` subprocesses the suite starts run it too.
FROM builder AS mutation
ENV UV_NO_DEV=0
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
    rm -rf .venv \
 && uv sync --locked --group mutation --no-install-project \
 && echo /app/src > "$(.venv/bin/python -c 'import sysconfig; print(sysconfig.get_path("purelib"))')/cogmo_skills_mutants.pth" \
 && install -d -o 1000 -g 1000 /app/mutants
COPY tests /app/tests/
COPY contract /app/contract/
ENV PATH="/app/.venv/bin:${PATH}" HOME=/tmp PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
USER 1000:1000

# The tools register's CPython checks run (design/skills.md → Register-time
# CPython checks): the skills repo toolchain's whole dev group, from the lock
# the repo commits, so it cannot drift from what `.cogmo/verify` runs. The
# builder's UV_NO_DEV=1 would drop the group; `--locked` fails a stale lock.
FROM builder AS tools
ENV UV_NO_DEV=0 UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/opt/cogmo-skills/tools
WORKDIR /toolchain
COPY toolchain/pyproject.toml toolchain/uv.lock /toolchain/
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
    uv sync --locked --only-group dev --no-install-project

# The toolchain's entries as the boot commits them to the skills repo: those
# `.cogmo/paths` lists, with `cogmo_ctx` joined into `.cogmo/`. The checks
# read their configuration here, the files the author's `.cogmo/verify` reads.
FROM builder AS toolchain
COPY toolchain /src/toolchain/
COPY src/cogmo_ctx /src/cogmo_ctx/
RUN install -d /opt/cogmo-skills/toolchain \
 && while read -r entry; do \
      [ -z "${entry}" ] || cp -a "/src/toolchain/${entry}" /opt/cogmo-skills/toolchain/; \
    done < /src/toolchain/.cogmo/paths \
 && cp -a /src/cogmo_ctx /opt/cogmo-skills/toolchain/.cogmo/cogmo_ctx \
 && find /opt/cogmo-skills/toolchain \( -name __pycache__ -o -name '*.py[co]' \) -prune -exec rm -rf {} +

FROM mirror.gcr.io/library/python:3.14.10-slim@sha256:af8a5aa14780025dbfbcfbc81bd8a91ebd87711dd5b0f48ed71090949dd7cb1d

ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

# `apt-get upgrade` applies Debian security updates that landed after
# the python:3.14-slim rebuild. Hadolint's DL3005 advises against this
# on the premise that maintainers keep base images patched; in practice
# the slim image trails Debian DSA advisories and this image runs inside
# sysbox sandboxes where every patch we can apply at build time tightens
# the userland surface. Cache cleanup keeps the runtime layer small.
# hadolint ignore=DL3005
RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get upgrade -y \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Nothing here uses the base image's pip: the supervisor and every skill run
# in venvs without system site-packages, and uv does all resolves and
# installs. Left installed, the copies it vendors (certifi, urllib3, msgpack,
# setuptools) would show in every scan, fixable only by a pip release.
RUN python3 -m pip uninstall --yes --root-user-action=ignore pip

# Non-root user (UID 1000, regular-user range — matches devbase's `vscode`
# user). Sysbox already maps the in-container root to a non-root host uid
# via user namespaces; this is defense in depth.
RUN useradd -m -u 1000 -s /bin/bash cogmo

# Copy just the venv from the builder, root-owned so `cogmo` can only read it.
# A task runs as `cogmo`, and the venv's `bin/` is first on PATH for the
# populate and reap scripts the host runs on a warm worker: a task able to
# write it could swap `python3` for code the next script runs. Nothing writes
# here at runtime; UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE precompiled the bytecode, and skill
# venvs live on /skill-venvs.
COPY --from=builder /app/.venv /opt/cogmo-skills/.venv
ENV PATH="/opt/cogmo-skills/.venv/bin:${PATH}"
ENV VIRTUAL_ENV="/opt/cogmo-skills/.venv"
# The venv links to the builder's interpreter, so a runtime FROM on another
# minor fails here rather than at the first task.
RUN "${VIRTUAL_ENV}/bin/python" --version

# uv in the runtime image too — the host runs `uv pip compile` at register
# and `uv venv` + `uv pip sync` at first invoke. Downloads stay off so they
# resolve on this image's Python instead of fetching another.
COPY --from=uv /uv /uvx /usr/local/bin/
ENV UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=0

# Pre-create /skill-venvs owned by `cogmo`. A fresh Docker named volume
# inherits this ownership on first mount, so the non-root supervisor
# can write into it without a CAP_CHOWN dance at runtime.
RUN mkdir -p /skill-venvs && chown cogmo:cogmo /skill-venvs

# The tools venv and the toolchain register's CPython checks read, root-owned
# like the runtime venv, with the bytecode UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE compiled. No
# PATH or sys.path names the tools venv: `cogmo_skills_runtime.check` runs
# each tool by its absolute path, and no task sees them.
COPY --from=tools /opt/cogmo-skills/tools /opt/cogmo-skills/tools
COPY --from=toolchain /opt/cogmo-skills/toolchain /opt/cogmo-skills/toolchain

# The release this toolchain belongs to, which a check reply carries. Last, so
# a version bump rebuilds this layer alone.
ARG VERSION=dev
RUN printf '%s\n' "${VERSION}" > /opt/cogmo-skills/VERSION

# Cogmo's host (`src/skills/worker-sysbox/worker.ts`) overrides the
# Entrypoint/Cmd at create-container time; the default below is for
# `docker run` smoke tests. WORKDIR is the user's home so any temp
# files the skill writes land somewhere writable.
USER cogmo
WORKDIR /home/cogmo
CMD ["python3", "-I", "-u", "-m", "cogmo_skills_runtime"]
